# DockerFile

Several functions on this page take keyword arguments and pass them on
to a command-line tool, and
[`mk_flags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#mk_flags)
does the conversion. A one-letter keyword becomes a short flag, so
`d=True` gives `-d` and `f='x'` gives `-f x`. A longer one becomes a
long flag with underscores turned into hyphens, so `remove_orphans=True`
gives `--remove-orphans` and `name='web'` gives `--name=web`. Keywords
set to `False` or `None` are left out, and positional arguments come
first. With `short=False`, every keyword becomes a long flag.

``` python
def mk_flags(

):
```

*Turn keyword arguments into command-line flags: one-letter keys become
`-k [value]` and longer keys `--key[=value]`.*

## Dockerfile instructions

A Dockerfile is a list of instructions, one per line, each starting with
a keyword such as `FROM`, `RUN` or `COPY`. The private helpers below
([`_from`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#_from),
[`_run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#_run),
[`_copy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#_copy) and so
on) each format one instruction. They take care of the details that are
easy to get wrong by hand: joining an image and its tag, writing a
command list in the JSON form Docker expects, and chaining several shell
commands into a single `RUN` with `&&`. You do not call them directly;
the
[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile)
methods do.

The tests after the helpers show the exact line each one writes.

``` python
assert _instr('RUN', 'echo hello') == 'RUN echo hello'
assert _from('python', '3.11') == 'FROM python:3.11'
assert _from('ubuntu', as_='builder') == 'FROM ubuntu AS builder'
assert _from('alpine') == 'FROM alpine'
assert _run('apt-get update') == 'RUN apt-get update'
r = _run(['apt-get update', 'apt-get install -y curl'])
assert 'apt-get update && ' in r
assert 'apt-get install -y curl' in r
assert _apt_install('curl', 'wget', y=True) == 'RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl wget && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*'
assert _apt_install('git', clean=False) == 'RUN apt-get update && apt-get install git'
assert _cmd(['python', 'app.py']) == 'CMD ["python", "app.py"]'
assert _cmd('echo hello') == 'CMD echo hello'
assert _copy('.', '/app') == 'COPY . /app'
assert _copy('/build/out', '/app', from_='builder') == 'COPY --from=builder /build/out /app'
assert _copy('app/', '.', link=True) == 'COPY --link app/ .'
assert _copy('/app', '/app', from_='builder', link=True) == 'COPY --from=builder --link /app /app'
assert _workdir('/app') == 'WORKDIR /app'
assert _env('PATH', '/usr/local/bin') == 'ENV PATH=/usr/local/bin'
assert _env('DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive') == 'ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive'
assert _expose(8080) == 'EXPOSE 8080'
assert _entrypoint(['python', '-m', 'flask']) == 'ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "flask"]'
assert _arg('VERSION', '1.0') == 'ARG VERSION=1.0'
assert _arg('VERSION') == 'ARG VERSION'
assert _label(version='1.0', maintainer='me') == 'LABEL version="1.0" maintainer="me"'
assert _volume('/data') == 'VOLUME /data'
assert _volume(['/data', '/logs']) == 'VOLUME ["/data", "/logs"]'
assert _shell(['/bin/bash', '-c']) == 'SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]'
assert 'CMD curl' in _healthcheck('curl -f http://localhost/', i='30s')
assert _healthcheck('curl localhost', i='30s', t='10s') == 'HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s CMD curl localhost'
assert _healthcheck('curl localhost') == 'HEALTHCHECK CMD curl localhost'
assert _on_build(_run('echo triggered')) == 'ONBUILD RUN echo triggered'
```

## The Dockerfile builder

[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile)
holds the instruction lines in order. It has one method per Dockerfile
keyword, named in lower case, and each method returns a new
[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile)
with the line added, so calls chain. `print` shows the file, and `save`
writes it, to `./Dockerfile` by default. A keyword without its own
method still works: `df.maintainer('me')` adds `MAINTAINER me`, and
`df('healthcheck', 'NONE')` does the same by name.

`run_mount` adds a `RUN` line with a `--mount` option. The default is a
cache mount, a folder such as pip’s download cache that Docker keeps
between builds; give its path as `target`.

[`_parse`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#_parse),
below, reads Dockerfile text into a list of lines. It joins lines
continued with a backslash and drops blank lines and comments, and
[`Dockerfile.load`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile.load)
uses it.

``` python
parsed = _parse("# comment\nFROM python:3.11\nRUN apt-get update && \\\n    apt-get install -y curl\nCOPY . /app")
print(parsed)
assert len(parsed) == 3
assert parsed[0] == 'FROM python:3.11'
assert 'apt-get install -y curl' in parsed[1]
```

    ['FROM python:3.11', 'RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl', 'COPY . /app']

``` python
def Dockerfile(
    items:NoneType=None, *rest, use_list:bool=False, match:NoneType=None
```

*Build a Dockerfile one instruction at a time; each method returns a new
Dockerfile.*

``` python
df = (Dockerfile().from_('python:3.11-slim')
    .run('pip install flask')
    .copy('.', '/app')
    .workdir('/app')
    .expose(5000)
    .cmd(['python', 'app.py']))

expected = """FROM python:3.11-slim
RUN pip install flask
COPY . /app
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 5000
CMD [\"python\", \"app.py\"]"""

print(df)
assert str(df) == expected
```

    FROM python:3.11-slim
    RUN pip install flask
    COPY . /app
    WORKDIR /app
    EXPOSE 5000
    CMD ["python", "app.py"]

``` python
df = (Dockerfile().from_('python:3.12-slim')
    .run_mount('pip install -r requirements.txt', target='/root/.cache/pip')
    .run_mount('uv sync --frozen', target='/root/.cache/uv')
    .run_mount('apt-get install -y curl', type='cache', target='/var/cache/apt'))
s = str(df)
assert "RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install -r requirements.txt" in s
assert "RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv uv sync --frozen" in s
print(df)
```

    FROM python:3.12-slim
    RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install -r requirements.txt
    RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv uv sync --frozen
    RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt apt-get install -y curl

A multi-stage build. Each `from_` starts a new stage, and
`copy(from_=...)` takes files from an earlier one:

``` python
df = (Dockerfile().from_('golang:1.21', as_='builder')
    .workdir('/src')
    .copy('.', '.')
    .run('go build -o /app')
    .from_('alpine')
    .copy('/app', '/app', from_='builder')
    .cmd(['/app']))

assert 'FROM golang:1.21 AS builder' in str(df)
assert 'COPY --from=builder /app /app' in str(df)
print(df)
```

    FROM golang:1.21 AS builder
    WORKDIR /src
    COPY . .
    RUN go build -o /app
    FROM alpine
    COPY --from=builder /app /app
    CMD ["/app"]

Pass a list to `run` to join several shell commands with `&&` into one
`RUN` line, which gives one image layer instead of several:

``` python
df = (Dockerfile().from_('ubuntu:22.04').run(['apt-get update', 'apt-get install -y python3', 'rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*']))
print(df)
```

    FROM ubuntu:22.04
    RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

### Loading an existing Dockerfile

[`Dockerfile.load`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile.load)
reads a Dockerfile from disk, so you can start from a file you already
have and add to it. `save` writes the file and returns the
[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile)
itself, not the path.

``` python
import tempfile
```

``` python
tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
Path(f'{tmp}/Dockerfile').write_text("# My app\nFROM python:3.11-slim\nRUN apt-get update && \\\n    apt-get install -y curl\nCOPY . /app\nCMD [\"python\", \"app.py\"]")

df = Dockerfile.load(f'{tmp}/Dockerfile')
assert len(df) == 4
assert df[0] == 'FROM python:3.11-slim'

p = f'{tmp}/Dockerfile'
df.save(p)
assert Path(p).exists()

df2 = df.run('echo hi')
assert len(df2) == 5
print(df)
```

    FROM python:3.11-slim
    RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
    COPY . /app
    CMD ["python", "app.py"]

## Build, run, test

These functions wrap the Docker command-line tool for the usual loop:
build an image from a
[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile),
run a container from it, and check that a command succeeds inside it.
They need Docker installed and its daemon running.

[`Cli`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#cli) is a small
base class for wrapping a command-line tool, and
[`Docker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#docker) is
the one for `docker`. Any attribute is a subcommand, with underscores
turned into hyphens, and keywords become flags: `Docker().ps(a=True)`
runs `docker ps -a`. Calling the object directly also works, as in
`Docker()('logs', 'web')`. Each call returns what the command printed
and raises `IOError` if it fails. `Docker().compose(...)` runs a compose
subcommand, using the older standalone `docker-compose` if it is
installed and `docker compose` otherwise.

`Docker(no_creds=True)` runs docker with a copy of your Docker config
that has the credential helpers (`credsStore` and `credHelpers`) taken
out, kept in `~/.fastops/config`. It applies only when the
`DOCKR_RUNTIME` environment variable is unset or set to `docker`.

[`Dockerfile.build`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile.build)
saves the Dockerfile into the folder `path` and builds it with
`docker compose build`. That command uses the daemon’s BuildKit and does
not need the buildx plugin. `build` returns the tag.
[`test`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#test) runs a
command in a throwaway container and returns `True` if the command exits
with status 0.
[`drun`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#drun) runs a
container and returns its output. With `detach=True` it starts the
container in the background and returns its ID. The `ports` dictionary
maps container ports to host ports.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>ports</code> entry</th>
<th>container port</th>
<th>host port</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>{'80/tcp': 8080}</code></td>
<td>80</td>
<td>8080</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

With `check=True`, the default,
[`drun`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#drun) watches
a detached container for up to two seconds. It raises `RuntimeError`,
with the container’s logs, if the container stops in that time.

### Convenience functions

Short wrappers for the commands used most.
[`containers`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#containers)
lists container names, running ones only unless you pass `all=True`.
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#images)
lists images as `repository:tag`.
[`logs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#logs) returns
the last `n` lines of a container’s log.
[`stop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#stop),
[`rm`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#rm) and
[`rmi`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#rmi) stop a
container, remove a container and remove an image, and `force=True` adds
`-f` to the last two.

### Example: a FastHTML app with uv

A Dockerfile for a [FastHTML](https://fastht.ml) app. It installs curl
and sqlite3 with apt, exports the dependencies from `pyproject.toml`
with uv and installs them with pip, and declares `/app/data` as a volume
so the app’s data is kept outside the container:

``` python
df = (Dockerfile().from_('python', '3.12-slim')
    .apt_install('curl', 'sqlite3', y=True)
    .run('pip install uv')
    .workdir('/app')
    .copy('pyproject.toml', '.')
    .run('uv export --no-hashes -o requirements.txt && pip install -r requirements.txt')
    .copy('.', '.')
    .volume('/app/data')
    .expose(5001)
    .cmd(['python', 'main.py']))

print(df)
```

    FROM python:3.12-slim
    RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl sqlite3 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    RUN pip install uv
    WORKDIR /app
    COPY pyproject.toml .
    RUN uv export --no-hashes -o requirements.txt && pip install -r requirements.txt
    COPY . .
    VOLUME /app/data
    EXPOSE 5001
    CMD ["python", "main.py"]

Building and running needs Docker, so the next cell is skipped in the
docs build. It builds a tiny image, runs it, prints what it printed, and
removes it:

``` python
tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
df = Dockerfile().from_('alpine').run('echo hello > /greeting.txt').cmd(['cat', '/greeting.txt'])
tag = df.build(tag='fastops-test:hello', path=tmp, no_creds=True)
print(f'Built: {tag}')
out = drun(tag, remove=True)
print(f'Output: {out}')
rmi(tag, force=True)
print('Cleaned up.')
```

    Built: fastops-test:hello
    Output: hello
    Cleaned up.

### End to end: a FastHTML todo app

This example writes a small todo app to a temporary folder, builds it
into an image, runs it, adds three todos through its web form and reads
them back from its JSON API. The first cell writes the app and defines
two helpers for later cells: `test_post` adds and lists the todos, and
`cleanup` removes the container and the image.

``` python
app_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'fasthtml-todo'
app_dir.mkdir()

code = {'main.py' :'''
from json import dumps
from fasthtml.common import *

db = database('data/todos.db')
todos = db.t.todos
if todos not in db.t: todos.create(id=int, title=str, done=bool, pk='id')
Todo = todos.dataclass()

app, rt = fast_app(live=False)

@rt('/')
def get():
    items = [Li(f"{'✓' if t.done else '○'} {t.title}", id=f'todo-{t.id}') for t in todos()]
    return Titled('Todos',
        Ul(*items),
        Form(Input(name='title', placeholder='New todo...'), Button('Add'), action='/add', method='post'))

@rt('/add', methods=['post'])
def post(title: str):
    todos.insert(Todo(title=title, done=False))
    return Redirect('/')

@rt('/api/todos')
def api():
    data = [dict(id=t.id, title=t.title, done=t.done) for t in todos()]
    return Response(dumps(data), media_type='application/json')

serve(host='0.0.0.0', port=5001)
''', 'requirements.txt':'python-fasthtml\n'}

for k,v in code.items(): Path(app_dir / k).write_text(v)

def test_post(url='http://localhost:5001'):
    for t in ['Buy milk', 'Write docs', 'Ship fastops']: urlread(f'{url}/add', title=t)
    for t in urljson(f'{url}/api/todos'): print(f"  {'✓' if t['done'] else '○'} {t['title']}")

def cleanup(nm, tag):
    rm(nm, force=True)
    rmi(tag, force=True)

print(f'App dir: {app_dir}')
print('Files:', os.listdir(app_dir))
```

    App dir: /var/folders/kg/9vdw4mdd1fs58svgh4k1qhr09x7dqh/T/tmphf0q8sp4/fasthtml-todo
    Files: ['requirements.txt', 'main.py']

``` python
df = (Dockerfile()
    .from_('python', '3.12-slim')
    .workdir('/app')
    .copy('requirements.txt', '.')
    .run('pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt')
    .copy('.', '.')
    .volume('/app/data')
    .expose(5001)
    .cmd(['python', 'main.py']))

print(df)
```

    FROM python:3.12-slim
    WORKDIR /app
    COPY requirements.txt .
    RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
    COPY . .
    VOLUME /app/data
    EXPOSE 5001
    CMD ["python", "main.py"]

``` python
import time
from fastcore.net import urlread, urljson
```

Building and running the app needs Docker, so the next cell is skipped
in the docs build. It removes any container left from an earlier run,
starts the app on port 5001, calls `test_post`, and cleans up:

``` python
tag = 'fastops-fasthtml:latest'
name = 'fastops-fasthtml-demo'
df.build(tag=tag, path=str(app_dir), no_creds=True)
print(f'Built: {tag}')
for cid in Docker()('ps', '-aq', '--filter', f'ancestor={tag}').splitlines(): rm(cid, force=True)
rm(name, force=True)
cid = drun(tag, detach=True, ports={'5001/tcp': 5001}, name=name, check=True)
print(f'Container: {cid[:12]}')
time.sleep(3)

try: test_post()
except Exception as e:
    print(f'Test failed: {e}')
    print(f'\nLogs:')
    print(logs(name, n=3))
finally: cleanup(name, tag)
print('Cleaned up.')
```

    Built: fastops-fasthtml:latest
    Container: bf1125b54374
      ○ Buy milk
      ○ Write docs
      ○ Ship fastops
    Cleaned up.

# Docker Compose

A Compose file, `docker-compose.yml`, lists the services that make up an
app and how they connect, and `docker compose up` starts them all
together. A service is one container in that stack, described by the
image it runs or the folder it is built from, plus its ports,
environment variables, volumes and the other services it needs.

## Service

[`service`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#service)
turns keyword arguments into the dict for one service. `ports` and
`volumes` can be dicts, `{host_port: container_port}` and
`{volume_or_host_path: container_path}`, which become Compose’s `"a:b"`
strings, and `env` can be a dict, which becomes `KEY=value` strings.
Lists are kept as they are. A
[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile)
passed as `build` becomes `build: .`. Save that Dockerfile in the folder
the Compose file runs from. Arguments left as `None` are omitted, and
any other keyword, such as `restart` or `networks`, is copied in
unchanged. You will usually call it through
[`Compose.svc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#compose.svc).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L230"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### service

``` python
def service(
    image:NoneType=None, build:NoneType=None, ports:NoneType=None, env:NoneType=None, volumes:NoneType=None,
    depends_on:NoneType=None, command:NoneType=None, **kw
):
```

*Return the dict for one Compose service, turning `ports`, `env` and
`volumes` dicts into Compose’s list form.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Compose

[`Compose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#compose)
builds the whole file. `svc` adds a service, passing its keywords to
[`service`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#service).
`network` and `volume` declare a network or a named volume, with any
keywords as its settings. Each call returns a new
[`Compose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#compose),
so calls chain. `print` shows the YAML, `to_dict` returns the same thing
as a dict, and `save` writes it, to `docker-compose.yml` by default.
[`Compose.load`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#compose.load)
reads an existing file back in.

`up` saves the file and runs `docker compose up`, detached unless you
pass `detach=False`. `down` and
[`logs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#logs) run
`docker compose down` and `docker compose logs` on the file that is
already saved. Extra keywords to all three become flags in the way
[`mk_flags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#mk_flags)
describes, and `no_creds=True` works as it does for
[`Docker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#docker).

### Compose

``` python
def Compose(
    items:NoneType=None, *rest, use_list:bool=False, match:NoneType=None
):
```

*Build a docker-compose.yml from services, networks and volumes; each
method returns a new Compose.*

``` python
dc = (Compose()
      .svc('web', image='nginx', ports={80: 80}, networks=['backend'])
      .svc('redis', image='redis:alpine')
      .svc('db', image='postgres:15', env={'POSTGRES_PASSWORD': 'secret'},
           volumes={'pgdata': '/var/lib/postgresql/data'})
      .network('backend').volume('pgdata'))

d = dc.to_dict()
assert 'networks' in d
assert 'volumes' in d
assert 'pgdata' in d['volumes']
print(dc)
```

        environment:
        - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret
        volumes:
        - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    networks:

    volumes:
      pgdata: null

## App builders

Five methods added to
[`Dockerfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#dockerfile)
install dependencies: `inst_uv`, `uv_deps`, `uv_project`, `with_uv` and
`packages`. The builders further down use them.

A single-stage Dockerfile installs dependencies in the final image. A
multi-stage Dockerfile installs dependencies in a builder stage and
copies the result into a separate runtime stage.

`inst_uv` is the single-stage way to install a Python project. It
installs uv with pip, copies `pyproject.toml` in, runs
`uv sync --no-dev` and puts the project’s `.venv` on the `PATH`. With
`req=True` it copies `requirements.txt` instead and installs it into the
system Python.

Three options make the single-stage install reproducible and quick to
rebuild. `lock=True` copies `uv.lock` too and syncs with `--frozen`. The
image then has exactly the versions in the lock file. `bytecode=True`
compiles the installed packages to bytecode in the image. The app then
does not compile them each time it starts. `deps_first=True` splits the
install in two layers: `uv_deps` syncs the dependencies alone, then
`uv_project` copies the project in and syncs it. Docker reuses the
dependency layer until `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` changes. A code
change rebuilds only the second half. `mid` runs commands between
dependency installation and project installation, such as a download the
app needs at run time. `compile` names source folders to compile to
bytecode after the project sync.

The single-stage recipe pulls only from Docker Hub and installs uv with
pip. The multi-stage recipe pulls uv’s image from `ghcr.io`, and
GitHub’s registry answers some hosting providers’ addresses with 403
Forbidden for anonymous pulls. A Hetzner server building a Compose stack
hit this. Use `multistage=False, lock=True` on such servers.

`with_uv` is the multi-stage way. It adds a build stage in uv’s image
that installs the dependencies pinned in `uv.lock`, with uv’s cache kept
between builds, and then starts the runtime stage from `image`. The
caller copies the result across, as
[`python_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#python_app)
does with `copy(wd, wd, from_='builder')`.

`packages` installs system packages with apt-get. Pass the names as
separate arguments, not as one list. With no names it does nothing. A
builder can write `.packages(*listify(pkgs))` without checking whether
`pkgs` is empty.

In
[`python_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#python_app),
`pkgs` installs apt packages, `pre` runs commands after them, `vols`
creates folders for volumes, and `healthcheck` adds a check on that
path. The check uses curl when `pkgs` installs it, and otherwise a
Python one-liner with `urllib`, since the slim image has no curl.
`ports=3` exposes three consecutive ports from `port`, for an app that
runs one worker per port; the health check probes the first. With
`multistage=False` it uses `inst_uv` in a single stage, and `req=True`
then installs `requirements.txt`; `req` has no effect on the default
two-stage build. `multistage=False, lock=True` is the locked
single-stage recipe: dependencies first from `uv.lock`, then the
project, with `bytecode`, `mid` and `compile` passed to `inst_uv`.
`fasthtml_app` is
[`python_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#python_app)
with `port=5001`, `cmd=['python', 'app.py']` and `multistage=False`
filled in by `bind`, and any of them can be overridden.
[`fastapi_react`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#fastapi_react)
expects the frontend in `frontend/` with its build output in `dist/`,
copies that to `/app/static`, runs `uvicorn main:app`, and by default
adds a health check on `/health`, chosen the same way.

[`detect_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#detect_app)
checks for `Cargo.toml`, then `go.mod`, then `package.json` (with or
without Python files), then `pyproject.toml` (with or without
`python-fasthtml` in it), then `requirements.txt`, and raises
`ValueError` if it finds none of them.

### Builder tests

The cells below check the lines that each builder writes.

``` python
df = Dockerfile().from_('python:3.13-slim').workdir('/app').inst_uv()
s = str(df)
assert 'pip install uv' in s
assert 'uv sync --no-dev' in s
assert 'ENV PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH' in s
assert 'COPY uv.lock' not in s
print('inst_uv OK')

df = Dockerfile().with_uv('ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm', 'python:3.13-slim', '/app')
s = str(df)
assert 'uv:python3.13-bookworm AS builder' in s
assert 'ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1' in s and 'ENV UV_LINK_MODE=copy' in s
assert 'FROM python:3.13-slim' in s
print('build_uv OK')

assert len(Dockerfile().from_('alpine').packages()) == 1   # no-op
assert 'apt-get install -y curl' in str(Dockerfile().from_('alpine').packages('curl'))
print('packages OK')

df = Dockerfile().from_('python:3.13-slim').workdir('/app').inst_uv(req=True)
s = str(df)
assert 'pip install uv' in s
assert 'COPY requirements.txt .' in s
assert 'uv pip install --system -r requirements.txt' in s
assert 'pyproject.toml' not in s and 'uv sync' not in s
assert 'ENV PATH' not in s
print('inst_uv(req=True) OK')
```

``` python
def _tmp(files):

    for f, c in files.items(): (d/f).write_text(c)
    return d

assert 'uvicorn' in str(detect_app(_tmp({'package.json': '{}', 'pyproject.toml': '[project]'})))
assert 'EXPOSE 5001' in str(detect_app(_tmp({'pyproject.toml': '[project]\ndependencies=["python-fasthtml"]'})))
assert 'EXPOSE 8000' in str(detect_app(_tmp({'pyproject.toml': '[project]'})))
s = str(detect_app(_tmp({'requirements.txt': 'flask\n'})))
assert 'uv pip install --system -r requirements.txt' in s and 'AS builder' not in s
try: detect_app(_tmp({'README.md': ''}))
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError('Expected ValueError')
print('detect_app() OK')
```

# Config and Secrets

## Non-secret config

Deploy scripts need values such as a server’s IP address or the path to
an SSH key.
[`env_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#env_set)
writes one to the file at the path `FASTOPS_ENV`. The default file is
`~/.config/fastops/.env`.
[`env_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#env_set)
creates a missing file with the permissions in the table.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>file mode</th>
<th>access</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>0600</td>
<td>the owner reads and writes, nobody else has access</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

[`env_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#env_set)
also sets the value in `os.environ`. The running process sees the value
at once.
[`env_get`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#env_get)
reads `os.environ` first, then the file, and returns `default` if
neither has the key. Both take `path` to use a different file. The test
below uses a temporary one; the “not found” lines are python-dotenv
reporting keys that are not in the file yet.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L417"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### env_get

``` python
def env_get(
    key, path:NoneType=None, default:NoneType=None
):
```

*Read `key` from `os.environ`, then the .env file, and return `default`
if neither has it.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L408"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### env_set

``` python
def env_set(
    key, value, path:NoneType=None
):
```

*Save `key=value` in the fastops .env file, or the file at `path`, and
in `os.environ`.*

``` python
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / '.env'
env_set('_FO_TEST_IP', '1.2.3.4', path=tmp)
assert os.environ['_FO_TEST_IP'] == '1.2.3.4'
assert env_get('_FO_TEST_IP', path=tmp) == '1.2.3.4'
env_set('_FO_TEST_IP', '1.2.3.4', path=tmp)
del os.environ['_FO_TEST_IP']
assert env_get('_FO_TEST_IP', path=tmp) == '1.2.3.4'
assert env_get('_FO_TEST_MISSING', path=tmp, default='fallback') == 'fallback'
env_set('_FO_TEST_IP', '5.6.7.8', path=tmp)
assert env_get('_FO_TEST_IP', path=tmp) == '5.6.7.8'
assert _FASTOPS_ENV is FASTOPS_ENV and FASTOPS_ENV.name == '.env'
print('env_set/env_get OK')
```

    Key _FO_TEST_IP not found in /var/folders/kg/9vdw4mdd1fs58svgh4k1qhr09x7dqh/T/tmp2xqc3991/.env.
    Key _FO_TEST_MISSING not found in /var/folders/kg/9vdw4mdd1fs58svgh4k1qhr09x7dqh/T/tmp2xqc3991/.env.

    env_set/env_get OK

## Secrets

[`secret_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_set)
and
[`secret_get`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_get)
are for sensitive values such as API tokens and tunnel tokens.
[`secret_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_set)
stores the value in the system keychain through the `keyring` package,
for example the macOS Keychain. Where there is no keychain, as on most
servers and CI machines, that step fails. By default (`save=False`)
[`secret_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_set)
then raises `RuntimeError` and writes nothing, because it never saves a
secret in plain text unless you ask. Pass `save=True` to also call
[`env_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#env_set),
which writes the value, in plain text, to the `.env` file and sets it in
`os.environ`. With `save=True` and no working keychain,
[`secret_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_set)
issues a `UserWarning` that names the `.env` file holding the only copy,
and still writes it.

[`secret_get`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_get)
looks in the keychain, then `os.environ`, then the `.env` file, and
returns `default` if none of them has the key. On a server, the usual
way to supply secrets is as environment variables, set at boot by
cloud-init or a systemd `EnvironmentFile=`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L435"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### secret_get

``` python
def secret_get(
    key, service:str='fastops', default:NoneType=None, path:NoneType=None
):
```

*Read a secret from the keychain, then `os.environ`, then the .env file,
and return `default` if none has it.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L425"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### secret_set

``` python
def secret_set(
    key, value, service:str='fastops', save:bool=False, path:NoneType=None
):
```

*Store a secret in the system keychain; with `save=True` also in the
.env file and `os.environ`, warning when that file holds the only copy;
raises `RuntimeError` if nothing stored it.*

``` python
secret_set('_FO_TEST_TOKEN', 'tok123', save=True)
assert os.environ.get('_FO_TEST_TOKEN') == 'tok123'
assert secret_get('_FO_TEST_TOKEN') == 'tok123'
del os.environ['_FO_TEST_TOKEN']
assert secret_get('_FO_TEST_MISSING_XYZ', default='fallback') == 'fallback'

# A key the keychain does not hold, so the environment has to answer for it. `get_password`
# returns None rather than raising, so a falsy result must fall through, not return.
os.environ['_FO_TEST_ENV_ONLY'] = 'from-environ'
assert secret_get('_FO_TEST_ENV_ONLY') == 'from-environ'
del os.environ['_FO_TEST_ENV_ONLY']
print('secret_set/secret_get OK')
```

    secret_set/secret_get OK

[`secrets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secrets)
reads several secrets at once and returns a dict of the keys that have a
value. Missing keys are left out without a warning.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L442"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### secrets

``` python
def secrets(
    *keys, service:str='fastops', path:NoneType=None
):
```

*Return a dict of the given secrets that have a value, leaving out the
missing ones.*

``` python
secret_set('_FO_TEST_A', 'val_a', save=True)
secret_set('_FO_TEST_B', 'val_b', save=True)

result = secrets('_FO_TEST_A', '_FO_TEST_B', '_FO_TEST_MISSING')
assert result == {'_FO_TEST_A': 'val_a', '_FO_TEST_B': 'val_b'}
print('secrets() OK')
```

    secrets() OK

# Skill install

dockeasy includes a `SKILL.md` file that describes its API to coding
agents.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies it into `.agents/skills/dockeasy/` and
`.claude/skills/dockeasy/`, where agent tools such as Claude Code look
for skills. The folders go under `dir` if you pass one, otherwise under
the root of the current git repository, which
[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#repo_root)
finds, otherwise under the current folder. By default it only prints
where it would copy the file; pass `dry_run=False` to copy it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L451"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### mv_skill_md

``` python
def mv_skill_md(
    dry_run:bool=True, dir:NoneType=None
)->None:
```

*Copy the bundled SKILL.md into the agent skill folders under `dir` or
the repository root; `dry_run=True` only prints the targets.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/dockeasy/blob/main/dockeasy/core.py#L447"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### repo_root

``` python
def repo_root()->pathlib.Path:
```

*Return the nearest folder at or above the current one that contains
`.git`, or None.*

``` python
import dockeasy.core
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
dockeasy.core.mv_skill_md(dry_run=True, dir=tmp)
dockeasy.core.mv_skill_md(dry_run=False, dir=tmp)
expected = (Path(dockeasy.core.__file__).parent/'SKILL.md').read_text()
assert (tmp/'.agents/skills/dockeasy/SKILL.md').read_text() == expected
assert (tmp/'.claude/skills/dockeasy/SKILL.md').read_text() == expected
print('mv_skill_md OK')
```

    Would copy /home/runner/work/dockeasy/dockeasy/dockeasy/SKILL.md to: ['/tmp/tmpxu1lnnsr/.agents/skills/dockeasy/SKILL.md', '/tmp/tmpxu1lnnsr/.claude/skills/dockeasy/SKILL.md']
    Installed -> ['/tmp/tmpxu1lnnsr/.agents/skills/dockeasy/SKILL.md', '/tmp/tmpxu1lnnsr/.claude/skills/dockeasy/SKILL.md']
    mv_skill_md OK

## Regression checks

These checks use stand-ins for Docker and the keychain. Numeric flag
values survive, `build` writes the Compose build section with the
Dockerfile name it was given,
[`drun`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#drun) keeps
the protocol in a port key, a failed keychain with `save=False` raises
instead of reporting success, and
[`Compose.load`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#compose.load)
keeps top-level keys such as
[`secrets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secrets).

``` python
import unittest.mock as um
import subprocess
```

``` python
test_eq(mk_flags(short=False, retries=1, quiet=0, rm=True, pull=False), ['--retries=1', '--quiet=0', '--rm'])

built = {}
def fake_run(cmd, **kw):
    built.update(yaml.safe_load(Path(cmd[cmd.index('-f')+1]).read_text())['services']['img']['build'])
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, b'', b'')
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
with um.patch('subprocess.run', fake_run): Dockerfile().from_('python').build(path=d, fn='Dockerfile.prod')
test_eq(built['dockerfile'], 'Dockerfile.prod')

sent = []
with um.patch.dict(globals(), _docker_cmd=lambda *a, **k: sent.append(a) or ''): drun('img', ports={'53/udp': 5353, 80: 8080})
test_eq([a for a in sent[0] if ':' in a], ['5353:53/udp', '8080:80'])

with um.patch.object(keyring, 'set_password', side_effect=RuntimeError('no keyring')):
    test_fail(lambda: secret_set('_FO_TEST_NOSTORE', 'x', path=Path(d)/'.env'), contains='save=True')
    test_fail(lambda: secret_set('_FO_TEST_NOSTORE', 'x', save=False, path=Path(d)/'.env'), contains='keychain')
test_eq((Path(d)/'.env').exists(), False)
test_eq('_FO_TEST_NOSTORE' in os.environ, False)

f = Path(d)/'dc.yml'
f.write_text('name: proj\nservices:\n  a: {image: x}\nsecrets:\n  s: {file: ./s.txt}\n')
list(Compose.load(f).to_dict())
```

The compose style is probed once, so later compose calls do not run
`docker-compose version` again.

``` python
probes, styles = [], []
_compose_cmd.cache_clear()
with um.patch.dict(globals(), run=lambda *a, **k: probes.append(a) or ''):
    styles += [_compose_cmd(), _compose_cmd()]
_compose_cmd.cache_clear()
test_eq(len(probes), 1)
styles
```

With an explicit `save=True` and no working keychain,
[`secret_set`](https://vedicreader.github.io/dockeasy/core.html#secret_set)
issues a `UserWarning` that names the `.env` file, and still writes the
value there. With the default `save=False` and no working keychain, it
raises `RuntimeError` and writes nothing.

``` python
env = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'.env'
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w, um.patch.object(keyring, 'set_password', side_effect=RuntimeError('no keychain')):
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    secret_set('_FO_TEST_WARN', 'v', save=True, path=env)
test_eq([str(env) in str(x.message) for x in w], [True])
test_eq(env_get('_FO_TEST_WARN', path=env), 'v')
del os.environ['_FO_TEST_WARN']
str(w[0].message)
```
